summary: Kept the witnessed over-compaction and bounded it with the same derivation rather than running another probe whose trigger the derivation excludes. The child account now states: with the recorded accepted indexes drifted to 10, 9 and 7 over six indices of content and every node's decided report drifted to 9, the public trim(None) returned no error and compacted index 7 — past the leader's own content — after which its reads of indices 5 and 6 reported Trimmed with a two-element decided-log read while the followers still reported accepted 10 and 7, and the declared comparison requiring the compacted index to reach the six decided indices was violated at the trim event. The new narrowing: both trim paths are bounded by the minimum recorded accepted index (the explicit-index path refuses anything above it and reports that minimum), so the bound can only exceed the content of replicas whose recorded value has itself drifted — a replica whose report is still truthful would lower the minimum — and since in the drifted cluster every recorded value sits at or above the compacted index, no in-cluster promise or log sync can ask for a prefix below it, so the underflow hazard I had sourced from the same lead is not reachable by that route. A fact records that bound property, the interpretation keeps conclusion violated with defect_claim asserted for the witnessed over-compaction while moving the hazard from untested to argued unreachable in this configuration, and the question's discriminator now asks whether any other producer (forwarded compaction, snapshot-driven compaction, a store-level trim) or any caller/storage route can raise a compacted index past a truthful replica's report or request a prefix below a compacted index. No execution was requested this turn; incomplete are that other-producer question, the parent drift's bound and reconfiguration-handoff questions, timers and loss triggers, larger clusters, snapshots, persistence, and any further independent lead.
